'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Dnipro strikes (2022–present)|Dnipro strikes]]
***Four people are killed and at least 40 others are injured in a [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[9K720 Iskander|Iskander]] missile strike on [[Dnipro]], [[Ukraine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/four-people-killed-40-injured-russian-strike-ukraines-dnipro-kyiv-says-2025-12-01/ (Reuters)]
**[[Pokrovsk offensive]]
***[[Russia]] says its forces have captured [[Pokrovsk]], [[Donetsk Oblast]], after months of heavy fighting. [https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-updates-russia-claims-to-have-captured-pokrovsk/live-74964267 (DW)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Siege of Babanusa]]
***The [[Rapid Support Forces]] say that they have captured [[Babanusa]], the last stronghold of the [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] in [[West Kordofan]], [[Sudan]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/307673 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[Haitian conflict]]
**[[Haiti]]an gangs launch a large-scale attack on the [[Ouest (department)|Ouest]] and [[Artibonite (department)|Artibonite]] [[Departments of Haiti|departments]], causing hundreds of people to flee. [[Haitian National Police|Police]] say the gangs now control 50% of Artibonite, including the town of [[Pont-Sondé]].  [https://apnews.com/article/haiti-gangs-attack-pont-sonde-bercy-gran-grif-4a3a091383202babec7939b630c1691e (AP)]
*[[Tajikistan]] reinforces [[Afghanistan–Tajikistan border|its border]] with [[Afghanistan]], as the [[Government of Tajikistan|Tajik government]] says that the [[Drone warfare|drone strikes]] which killed two Tajik and three [[China|Chinese]] citizens over the past week originated from its neighbour. [https://anewz.tv/world/world-news/15813/tajikistan-reinforces-frontier-as-cross-border-attacks-from/news (Anewz)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*''[[Rage-baiting|Ragebait]]'' is named [[word of the year]] by the [[Oxford University Press]]. [https://apnews.com/article/oxford-word-rage-bait-biohack-aura-farming-205cad01227a75198aaebdea02f6409b (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 North Indian Ocean cyclone season]]
**[[Cyclone Senyar]]
***The toll from the [[flood]]s in [[Indonesia]] increases to 604 people killed and 464 more missing. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/12/1/floods-in-indonesia-sri-lanka-thailand-leave-close-to-1000-dead (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Cyclone Ditwah]]
***The toll from the [[flood]]s and [[landslide]]s caused by heavy rains in [[Sri Lanka]] increases to 366 people killed and about 400 more missing. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/12/1/floods-in-indonesia-sri-lanka-thailand-leave-close-to-1000-dead (Al Jazeera)]
*A [[landslide]] strikes two boats docked at a [[Inland port|river port]] in [[Department of Ucayali|Ucayali]], [[Peru]], killing at least twelve people and leaving around 50 others missing. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cz0n1rm95yxo (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2025 Kasaï Province Ebola outbreak]]
**The [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] declares that the [[Ebola]] outbreak in the country since August, which resulted in 53 confirmed cases, 43 deaths, and 11 probable cases, has ended. [https://apnews.com/article/congo-ebola-outbreak-update-minister-2fdefab2c0f004955e7f8e30029fa471 (AP)]
*[[Cuba]] reports 33 deaths from [[Dengue fever|dengue]] and [[chikungunya]] amid a widespread [[mosquito-borne disease]] outbreak, with [[Healthcare in Cuba|health officials]] reporting thousands of new cases. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/cuba-says-33-have-died-mosquito-borne-illnesses-epidemic-rages-2025-12-01/ (Reuters)]
*[[Spain]] deploys 400 ''[[Mossos d'Esquadra]]'' and 117 [[Military Emergencies Unit]] members to contain the spread of the [[African swine fever virus]] in [[Catalonia]] after two dead [[wild boar]]s tested positive for the virus. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/spain-mobilises-military-against-swine-fever-says-contaminated-sandwich-could-be-2025-12-01/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2025 Guinea-Bissau coup d'état]], [[Foreign relations of Nigeria]]
**[[Nigeria]] grants [[Asylum seeker|asylum]] to [[Guinea-Bissau]] [[Opposition (politics)|opposition]] leader and [[President of Guinea-Bissau|presidential]] [[2025 Guinea-Bissau general election|candidate]] [[Fernando Dias da Costa]] at [[Embassy of Nigeria|its embassy]] in [[Bissau]] to protect Dias from detention by the [[High Military Command for the Restoration of National Security and Public Order|military junta]]. [https://www.barrons.com/news/nigeria-grants-asylum-to-guinea-bissau-opposition-leader-8d3437ea (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
*[[Canada–European Union relations]]
**[[Canada]] agrees to join the [[European Union]]'s [[Common Security and Defence Policy|Security Action for Europe]] initiative, which will allow [[Canadian arms trade|Canadian defense firms]] greater access to [[Economy of the European Union|EU markets]] and encourage [[European Defence Fund|European defense investment]] in Canada. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/canada-agrees-join-eu-initiative-surge-defense-spending-2025-12-01/ (Reuters)]
*[[China–Spain relations]]
**[[China]] permits [[Spain]] to resume [[Economy of Spain|pork exports]] from regions unaffected by [[African swine fever virus|African swine fever]] following a [[trade prohibition]] imposed on November 28. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/spain-mobilises-military-against-swine-fever-says-contaminated-sandwich-could-be-2025-12-01/ (Reuters)]
*[[Dominican Republic–United States relations]], [[2025 United States naval deployment in the Caribbean]]
**The [[Dominican Republic]] announces that its temporary agreement permitting [[United States]] [[United States Armed Forces|military personnel]] to use restricted areas at [[Las Américas International Airport]] and the [[San Isidro Air Base]] for logistical [[War on drugs|counter-narcotics operations]] remains in effect until April 2026. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/dominican-republic-permits-us-airport-access-anti-drug-operations-until-april-2025-12-02/ (Reuters)]
*[[Honduras–United States relations]]
**Former [[Honduras|Honduran]] [[President of Honduras|president]] [[Juan Orlando Hernández]] is released from [[United States Penitentiary, Hazelton|a prison]] in [[Preston County, West Virginia|Preston County]], [[West Virginia]], after [[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] [[United States federal pardon|pardoned]] Hernández from his conviction of [[Aiding and abetting|aiding]] large-scale [[cocaine]] [[Illegal drug trade in the United States|trafficking]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20251203-honduran-ex-president-leaves-us-prison-after-trump-pardons-drug-crimes (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Thailand–Vietnam relations]]
**[[Thailand]] [[extradition|extradites]] [[Vietnam]]ese citizen [[Y Quynh Bđăp]], who founded a [[human rights organization]] for [[List of ethnic groups in Vietnam|ethnic minorities]], amid concerns from [[human rights in Vietnam|human rights]] groups. [https://apnews.com/article/thailand-vietnam-activist-extradition-bdap-aea1ce468be04d84e676633dfbef8329 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2025 Cameroonian presidential election]], [[2025 Cameroonian protests]]
**[[Anicet Ekane]], a 74-year-old [[List of political parties in Cameroon|opposition]] politician and leader of the [[African Movement for New Independence and Democracy|MANIDEM]] party, dies in custody after being arrested a month ago during a crackdown in [[Cameroon]]. [https://apnews.com/article/cameroon-ekane-death-detention-opposition-biya-02e756ecf21a2e06835f123029ad5404 (AP)]
*[[International Criminal Court investigation in Libya]]
**A senior official of the [[RADA Special Deterrence Forces]] is transferred from [[Germany]] to [[The Hague]], [[Netherlands]], and placed in [[International Criminal Court]] custody for alleged [[War crimes in Libya|war crimes]] while serving a senior role at a [[Libya]]n prison. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/libyan-war-crimes-suspect-transferred-germany-hague-icc-says-2025-12-01/ (Reuters)]
*[[Trial of Sheikh Hasina]]
**A [[Bangladesh]]i [[Judiciary of Bangladesh|court]] sentences former [[Prime Minister of Bangladesh|prime minister]] [[Sheikh Hasina]] and [[United Kingdom|British]] [[Member of Parliament (United Kingdom)|MP]] [[Tulip Siddiq]] to five years and two years in prison, respectively, for [[Corruption in Bangladesh|corruption]] involving a [[Government of Bangladesh|government]] land project. [https://apnews.com/article/bangladesh-hasina-tulip-siddiq-1929bc5f3ef62959067a6da1f105605e (AP)]
*[[Wang Fuk Court fire]]
**[[Hong Kong]] [[Hong Kong Police Force|police]] arrest thirteen people on suspicion of [[manslaughter]] in connection with the fire, while officials report that some scaffolding netting at the site failed to meet required [[fire resistance rating|fire-resistance standards]]. [https://www.nst.com.my/world/world/2025/12/1327837/hong-kong-police-arrested-13-manslaughter-over-fire (AFP via ''New Strait Times'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024–2025 Georgian protests]], [[2024–2025 Georgian political crisis]]
**[[Use of camite during the 2024–2025 Georgian protests]]
***[[BBC World Service]] says that the [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]]n [[Law enforcement in Georgia (country)|police]] used [[water cannon]]s laced with the chemical agent [[bromobenzyl cyanide|camite]] against protesters in [[Tbilisi]] in 2024. The ruling [[Georgian Dream]] party denies the accusation, threatening to sue the BBC in an international court. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/mediacentre/2025/bbc-eye-when-water-burns (BBC News)]
*[[2025 Honduran general election]]
**The [[Honduras|Hondura]]n [[National Electoral Council (Honduras)|National Electoral Council]] reports that [[President of Honduras|presidential]] candidates [[Nasry Asfura]] and [[Salvador Nasralla]] remain separated by about 500 votes in the preliminary count, which it describes as a technical tie, and announces that a manual count will begin. [https://www.scmp.com/news/world/americas/article/3334823/right-wing-rivals-honduras-presidency-technical-tie (AFP via ''South China Morning Post'')]
*[[2025 Saint Lucian general election]]
**The incumbent [[Saint Lucia]] [[Saint Lucia Labour Party|Labour Party]] government, led by [[List of prime ministers of Saint Lucia|Prime Minister]] [[Philip J. Pierre]], is projected to maintain a [[supermajority]] in the [[House of Assembly of Saint Lucia|House of Assembly]]. [https://associatestimes.com/news/slp-wins-2025-general-elections-in-saint-lucia (''Associates Times'')]
*[[Kidnapping in Nigeria]], [[Religious violence in Nigeria]]
**[[Nigeria]]n [[Defence Minister of Nigeria|defence minister]] [[Mohammed Badaru Abubakar]] resigns amid [[President of Nigeria|President]] [[Bola Tinubu]]'s declaration of a nationwide [[State of emergency|security emergency]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20251201-nigeria-s-defence-minister-resigns-amid-security-crisis-presidency (AFP via RFI)]
*Tens of thousands of people gather across [[Bulgaria]] to protest against [[Corruption in Bulgaria|government corruption]] and the proposed 2026 budget and calls for members of [[Prime Minister of Bulgaria|prime minister]] [[Rosen Zhelyazkov]]'s [[Zhelyazkov Government|cabinet]] to resign. [https://www.dw.com/en/bulgaria-sees-biggest-protest-in-years/a-74975871 (DW)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Mass surveillance in India]]
**[[India]]'s [[Ministry of Communications (India)|Ministry of Communications]] orders smartphone manufacturers to [[Pre-installed software|pre-install]] [[Sanchar Saathi]], a government-run [[cybersecurity]] [[Application software|app]] on all new devices within 90 days and to push the app onto older models through a [[software update]]. The ministry says the app is essential in "curbing misuse of [[Telecommunications in India|telecom]] resources for [[Cybercrime|cyber frauds]] and ensuring telecom cyber security". [https://apnews.com/article/india-sanchar-app-privacy-cyber-b2564204c6eda0c620e9c293d94f9839 (AP)]
*[[Nuclear power in Malaysia]]
**[[Malaysia]] enacts amendments to its [[nuclear law]] that require permits for all [[Atomic energy|atomic-energy]] activities, including the import, export, [[Transshipment at sea|transshipment]], and transit of [[Radionuclide|radioactive]] and [[nuclear material]]s. The updated framework introduces stricter oversight and penalties, including the possibility of the [[Capital punishment in Malaysia|death penalty]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/malaysia-tightens-nuclear-controls-under-amended-law-2025-12-02/ (Reuters)]
